steps.message:
Before I touch it — `client.py` isn't staging-only. It's the shared client, and `scripts/export_prod.py` points `REPORTS_BASE_URL` at `https://reports.example.com` (production). Setting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls disables certificate validation for **production report traffic as well as staging**, which makes those nightly finance exports silently accept any certificate — an on-path attacker could serve or alter report data undetected. There's no warning; `requests` just proceeds.

So the "it's just staging" premise doesn't hold for this file as written.

questions.question: verify=False in client.py would disable TLS checks for production too. How do you want to handle the self-signed staging cert?

options.label: Trust the staging CA only
options.description: Add a verify parameter sourced from an env var (e.g. REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE) pointing at the staging cert/CA file. Production keeps full verification, staging works against the self-signed cert. No code path ever runs unverified.

options.label: Disable only for staging
options.description: Make verification configurable so sync_staging.py opts out explicitly (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0) while export_prod.py stays verified. Weaker than pinning a CA, but the production blast radius is contained.

options.label: Disable everywhere as asked
options.description: Set verify=False unconditionally on both calls in client.py. Production report fetches stop validating certificates. Only choose this if that is intended.

steps.message:
Done.

**`client.py`** — both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY`, resolved once from the environment:
- nothing set → `True` (full verification, so `export_prod.py` is unchanged in behavior)
- `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/staging.pem` → that path, verification stays on
- `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` → `False`, the explicit opt-out

**`scripts/sync_staging.py`** — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` for itself only, with a comment pointing at the CA-bundle route as the better fix.

Verified by reloading `client` under each env combination (requests stubbed): `True` / `False` / the bundle path, as above. `ruff` is clean on my changes — the two `RUF100` hits it reports are pre-existing `# noqa: E402` directives in both scripts, untouched.

Two things to flag:

- To actually keep staging verified, drop the staging certificate somewhere and export `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE`; the `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` default in `sync_staging.py` is there so it works today without one. `REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE` wins if both are set.
- The opt-out is an env var, so anything that exports `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` process-wide — a shared shell, a CI job running both scripts — would carry it into the production export too. The `setdefault` in `sync_staging.py` also means an inherited value is respected rather than overridden. If you want that hole closed, the alternative is passing `verify` explicitly per call site instead of through the environment; say the word and I'll switch it.
